name: London Hot-Cross Buns
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: one cup of yeast, or one cake of compressed yeast dissolved in a cup of tepid water
ingredients.originalText: one cup of yeast, or one cake of compressed yeast dissolved in a cup of tepid water
ingredients.quantityText: one cup of yeast, or one cake of compressed yeast dissolved in a cup of tepid water

ingredients.name: melted butter
ingredients.originalText: half a cup of melted butter

instructions.text: Use flour enough to make a thick batter with milk and yeast
Set this as a sponge over night
In the morning add half a cup of melted butter, one cup of sugar, half a nutmeg grated, one saltspoonful of salt, and half a teaspoonful of soda
Add flour enough to roll out like biscuit
Knead well and set to rise for five hours
Roll the dough half an inch thick
Cut in round cakes and lay in rows in a buttered baking-pan
Let the cakes stand half an hour, or until light
Put them in the oven, having first made a deep cross on each with a knife
Bake a light brown and brush over with white of egg beaten stiff with powdered sugar

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Use flour enough to make a thick batter with milk and yeast
2. Set this as a sponge over night
3. In the morning add half a cup of melted butter, one cup of sugar, half a nutmeg grated, one saltspoonful of salt, and half a teaspoonful of soda
4. Add flour enough to roll out like biscuit
5. Knead well and set to rise for five hours
6. Roll the dough half an inch thick
7. Cut in round cakes and lay in rows in a buttered baking-pan
8. Let the cakes stand half an hour, or until light
9. Put them in the oven, having first made a deep cross on each with a knife
10. Bake a light brown and brush over with white of egg beaten stiff with powdered sugar
